name: german-site
description: A well-built nine-page German SaaS site (Kontor Analytik GmbH), lang="de" throughout. The non-English coverage fixture: German call-to-action words, a street-then-number address (Hauptstrasse 12, 10115 Berlin), German opening hours, a Presse page, and German navigation labels. Guards the rule that a site written in another language must not be reported as missing the things this audit only knows how to look for in English.

expected.notes:
The point of this fixture is what PASSES; every entry in pass_required below would have fired before the non-English work.
en.cta.missing passes only because CTA_VOCAB_BY_LANG['de'] matches 'Jetzt registrieren' / 'Kostenlos testen' / 'Anmelden'. nap_missing_plain_text passes only because STREET_REVERSED_RE reads 'Hauptstrasse 12' -- the Anglo number-then-street grammar could never match it. press_page_missing passes only because PRESS_RE learned 'Presse' (note  press  cannot match 'Presse': the trailing 'e' is a word character). no_visible_dates passes off the ISO datetime attributes on /blog and /presse -- German written dates like '14.05.2026' are still not parsed, which is why the time elements carry datetime. The category resolves to saas_software from German nav labels (preise, funktionen, anmelden, registrieren).
The two language-gated checks are the honest half. The audience phrase is 'Software fuer Steuerberaterinnen und Steuerberater' and the English AUDIENCE_RE cannot see it, so fx.facts.key_fact_missing would otherwise fire on the missing audience fact -- but apply_language_gate withdraws it entirely (not_evaluated, reason language_not_supported) rather than reporting a weakened claim about a site it cannot read in its own language. fx.content.faq_absent is the same case: German FAQ headings are not in the English FAQ vocabulary, so the check has no verdict rather than a false 'no FAQ'. If either ever reports a fail or a finding here, the gate has broken.
breadcrumbs_missing, site_search_missing and related_links_missing are genuine and language-neutral: the site has neither, and its Funktionen page (sampled as the product role once the sampler learned that nav word) offers one onward link. Their presence in `fail` alongside the withdrawn checks is the language gate's promise made testable: everything that is actually a defect stays a defect, and everything the audit cannot read in German gets no verdict instead of a guess.
